case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread covers Bluetooth SIG RF and RF PHY qualification planning, pricing, execution, and troubleshooting for a BLE product expanding toward BR/EDR/BLE support. The discussion includes qualification scope decisions for LE 1M, 2M, Coded PHY, and Stable Modulation Index options, along with related cost impacts. Later exchanges focus on RF PHY test execution failures caused by Direct Test Mode communication mismatches and incorrect test tool usage. The issue was eventually resolved by switching to Serial-HCI mode and removing an interfering FCC-oriented utility from the RF PHY qualification workflow.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The consultant clarified that RF PHY testing scope depends on the actual supported PHY capabilities, allowing 1M-only qualification if the product only supports LE 1M PHY. Additional features such as 2M PHY, LE Coded PHY, and Stable Modulation Index significantly increase RF PHY test item count and cost. Stable Modulation Index testing was explained as a much tighter GFSK modulation accuracy requirement that depends largely on intrinsic SoC RF quality and may provide little practical value. During testing, RF PHY command-response failures were traced to incorrect use of Two-Wire mode, UART communication assumptions, and simultaneous use of an FCC-oriented utility that disrupted COM port routing between the InterLab tester and DUT. Final validation confirmed that the DUT responded correctly in Serial-HCI mode and RF PHY 1M testing successfully passed after correcting the workflow.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: Bluetooth qualification scope must align with the actual declared and supported PHY capabilities of the implementation. Optional PHY features should only be qualified when product requirements justify the additional test burden. RF PHY qualification depends on successful Direct Test Mode communication between the tester and DUT, so the tester communication mode must match the DUT implementation. External regulatory utilities that interfere with tester COM port ownership or serial routing can invalidate RF PHY testing even when the DUT itself functions correctly.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Declaring unnecessary PHY capabilities can increase qualification cost, RF PHY test scope, and scheduling complexity without product benefit. Running optional Stable Modulation Index testing without a clear requirement can create avoidable failures tied to SoC RF limitations that may not be fixable late in development. Incorrect DTM communication settings, UART wiring assumptions, or conflicting COM port tools can produce repeated RF PHY timeout failures, wasted lab time, retesting delays, and unnecessary escalation with the IC vendor. Mixing FCC-oriented tooling into the SIG qualification workflow can block tester-to-DUT communication and lead to false conclusions that the DUT itself is defective.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: The consultant later acknowledged that the test team incorrectly installed and used the FCC_assist1.0.4.exe regulatory support utility together with the InterLab RF PHY qualification system. This created conflicting COM port handling and broke the serial communication path between the RF PHY tester and DUT. Earlier assumptions also relied too heavily on the originally declared Two-Wire configuration without fully validating Serial-HCI behavior. The issue was corrected by removing FCC_assist from the workflow entirely and rerunning RF PHY qualification directly through the InterLab system in Serial-HCI mode.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always validate the DUT Direct Test Mode communication path independently before RF PHY qualification testing, and ensure the tester communication mode exactly matches the DUT implementation. Keep Bluetooth SIG qualification workflows isolated from FCC or other regulatory RF utilities unless compatibility is explicitly verified. Limit qualification scope to the PHY capabilities actually required by the product to reduce unnecessary testing cost, complexity, and failure exposure.
